notes: LARP (Linked Avatar Registry Protocol) on Ethereum, README v2, in the listed order. PlaceLARP takes no constructor argument: its constructor creates LARPBurner, LARP and IMDNames. PlaceLinks takes only the earlier PlaceLARP deployment and creates LARPLinks over the registry, names and burner it reads from that placer. No IMD protocol address is a launch argument: every address, fee, spacing and salt the four constructors receive is a constant of src/place/LARPPlan.sol (CreateX 0xba5Ed099633D3B313e4D5F7bdc1305d3c28ba5Ed; PoolManager, $IMD, IMD6900, the hooks, IDENTITY, ARTIST, INTAKE, ORACLE_SIGNER, LAUNCHER). Each placer uses CreateX's CREATE3 with the mined salts so the contracts land at the planned addresses: LARPBurner 0x69006faEc2D2094e375cAFA5e3C87C5cB2847bef, LARP 0x69000A4A9FA561Dd6b313741bf1F79F4aDE4adAF, IMDNames 0x690084D1331F7a6509EeD32e7d34ffAcB377d807, LARPLinks 0x69005EdeC64B8586EC8d5E32f757a818b5d493C0. A planned address someone used first is never taken: a salt whose CreateX proxy or destination already has code, or a chain without CreateX, falls back to the placer's own CREATE3 for the same contract at an address nobody could know beforehand. Read burner, larp and names from PlaceLARP and links from PlaceLinks for the actual addresses. No contract has an owner, role or upgrade path; the placers hold nothing and do nothing after construction. Prices and the IMD6900 share (6.9% at launch, 0-100%) change only by the swarm's verdict within the guardrails in IMDNames; $IMD not spent on IMD6900 goes to IMD's BurnExecutor (LARPBurner.IMD_BURN, a constant), never 0xdEaD; out-of-gas swaps revert. Deployment sends no ETH and makes no initialization call.
